title: Efteling offers new safety solution for coaster fans
summary:
By Robert Niles: Efteling is offering a new safety solution for thrill ride fans with leg prostheses.

The park's new SafeStrap allows visitors with leg prostheses to ride several park attractions without having to remove their prosthesis. The device will be available starting October 1 for riders on the floorless dive coaster Baron 1898, the Hooghmoed free-fall towers, and the park's swing rides. The new Ravenring attraction also will use the device when that ride opens December 1.


Riders using SafeStrap on Baron 1989. Photo courtesy Efteling

Let's talk about thrill ride restraint systems for a moment. The general concept is to develop a restraint system that can accommodate as many riders as possible while allowing operators to unload, load and dispatch the ride vehicle as quickly as possible.

That typically leads designers to a one-style-for-all solution, where all the seats on a train or ride employ the same system. That makes it easy for operators to load and dispatch, as all they need to do is check that riders have engaged the restraint, whether that's a lap bar, seatbelt, or over-the-shoulders pulldown bar. There's no need to customize the restraint offered for each rider.

Prospective riders who cannot be accommodated by the ride's restraint system would be excluded from the ride. Most often, that means a minimum rider height. But in some cases, that also has meant that people with a leg prosthesis, for example, would not be allowed to ride without removing it, given that the default restraint may not be able to secure the prosthesis.

Efteling's device removes that restriction. But it does so with an extra device that must be put on before the ride can dispatch. The challenge here is whether that has enough of a detrimental effect on load time that it reduces ride capacity to a significant extent.

The percentage of the population with leg prostheses is low - less than 1 percent. And I suspect that the percentage is even lower within the thrill ride community. So the time to get on and off a ride with the SafeStrap might easily get lost in the noise of variance among different hundreds of other riders' natural load and unload times. The downside then to the general population of coaster riders might be low, but the upside to a fan with a prothesis could be huge.

"From the very beginning, we worked together with prosthesis users, healthcare professionals and Efteling to develop a solution that is both safe and practical for users and amusement parks," said India Hoekman, who developed SafeStrap as part of her graduation project at Delft University of Technology. "I find it incredibly special that the product I designed as part of my final-year project is actually being used now."

Following its launch at Efteling, the SafeStrap is now available worldwide to theme parks and prosthetic users.

title: Step back to EPCOT's old American Gardens Theatre
summary:
By Robert Niles: Following the theme park home movies that I shared with you last week, I have another view into the past today. And this time, it's from Walt Disney World.

Today's video comes from EPCOT and features the 1989 Disney All-American College Orchestra. Long-time Theme Park Insider readers might remember that ensemble included the future Mrs. Theme Park Insider in the violin section. This video, linked below, captures a show with special guest Rosemary Clooney, a legendary singer whose fame these days has been eclipsed by her nephew, Academy Award-winner George Clooney.

Back in 1989, Disney had not yet built the shell that now covers the stage at the American Gardens Theatre and obscures the World Showcase Lagoon views. I understand the logistical considerations that prompted Disney to build the shell. Inclement weather cost too many showtimes, and guest artists began demanding more sophisticated lighting controls that were not possible on the open-air stage.

But that stage delivered an aesthetic that I miss - a visual connection with the rest of the park. I miss not seeing Spaceship Earth and the rest of the World Showcase as the background when watching a show in this theater. That was a unique visual environment that Disney has replaced with a generic and claustrophobic back wall that could be anywhere.

Disney also no longer has an All-American College Orchestra. Guest musical artists now populate EPCOT's spring and fall food festival events. The summer, when college musicians are available to relocate to Orlando, is no longer the high season at the resort. And too few musical acts anymore have shows prepared to perform with live orchestras, anyway. Still, watching those that do play the Hollywood Bowl here in Los Angeles, it's easy to miss the even more intimate experience that EPCOT once offered.

For a brief trip back in time to a night like that, please enjoy this video: Summer Orchestra Rosemary Clooney Concert 1989.

You can see the future Mrs. Laurie Niles sitting at the far left in the front row of the violins, starting at the 0:59 mark. This also happens to be the one College Orchestra performance from that summer attended by my parents, even though I had not met Laurie yet. My mother grew up in Covington, Kentucky, which also was the Clooneys' home town. (I was probably wrapping up a shift at Tom Sawyer Island over in the Magic Kingdom as this show started, so I am not here.) Adding to the serendipity, the daughter of the videographer who captured this performance ended up in the same high school cinematic arts program in Los Angeles as my son.

Clearly, Walt Disney World was the place to be in the summer of 1989!

title: Six Flags buys ArieForce One
summary:
By Robert Niles: We now know the mystery buyer that has obtained ArieForce One. It's Six Flags.

Six Flags announced this morning that it has purchased the acclaimed Rocky Mountain Construction roller coaster. The coaster closed last month along with its Fun Spot America Atlanta home park. Last week, owner John Arie Jr. announced that the family had found a buyer for the coaster.

What Six Flags has not yet announced, however, is which of its parks will be getting the 3,400-foot steel coaster. But Six Flags did confirm that it will retain the coaster's ArieForce One name.

"From the moment ArieForce One closed, we knew how much this coaster meant to the enthusiast community and to guests who traveled from around the world to experience it," Six Flags COO Mark Pauls said. "This is a ride that consistently generated excitement, acclaim and passionate fan support. We are thrilled to preserve its legacy, invest in its future and bring this extraordinary attraction to a new generation of guests. This acquisition represents our commitment to delivering world-class thrills and creating unforgettable experiences across the Six Flags portfolio."

"When we built ArieForce One, we wanted to create something truly special," John Arie Jr said. "Seeing ArieForce One preserved and finding a new home with Six Flags means a great deal to me and my family. Its story isn�t ending, it�s beginning a new chapter, and we are excited that future generations will get to experience ArieForce One."

title: Six Flags offers new payment plans for season passes
summary:
By Robert Niles: Six Flags is offering a new payment plan for its season passes. But unlike many other parks' plans, this one could end up costing you far more than the list price of a pass.

The new payment plan is called Flex Pay and it is offered via Six Flags' partnership with finance company Upgrade. Flex Pay is now available for select online purchases of $49 or more, including season passes.

"Six Flags has long been committed to providing families with one of the best entertainment values available," Six Flags Chief Marketing Officer Amy Martin Ziegenfuss said. "Flex Pay gives guests another way to maximize that value by locking in current pricing, breaking payments into manageable installments and enjoying a season of world-class rides, seasonal events and experiences from day one."

Flex Pay is a distinct product from Six Flags' monthly payment membership plans. With Flex Pay, you are getting an installment loan on the price of a season pass, which has an expiration date, until memberships, which are on-going.

Rivals such as Disney and Universal have offered payment plans on their annual passes, which typically cost far more than Six Flags' season passes. But those rivals have offered zero-interest payment plans. Six Flags' Flex Pay may charge interest for its payment plans, depending upon your personal credit history. And those interest rates may range up to 36% annually, according to Six Flags' website.

I am not a financial advisor, but paying any amount of interest on a theme park ticket purchase seems insane to me. And charging 36% on any loan outta be illegal, IMHO. If you are a fan who wants to visit regularly and can't afford to spend hundreds of dollars up front for a season pass, just get a Six Flags membership and its relatively low monthly payments.

Locking in a season pass price with a loan is only worth it if you are getting a zero-interest loan. Otherwise, the accrued interest effectively raises the price of that season pass, perhaps by even more than a future price increase if you had waited to pay in full at a later date.

I can only imagine that this is an example of the decoy effect, to make Six Flags memberships look even more attractive when compared with the payment plans on season passes. But financial illiteracy is a thing, so... anyway, that's what Six Flags announced today.

title: New Harry Potter theme park lands set for 2029 debut
summary:
By Robert Niles: Harry Potter and theme park fans have a new reason to look forward to 2029. That's the year that Warner Bros. World on Yas Island has targeted for the opening of its three new Harry Potter-themed lands.

Yas Island developer Miral announced that target date today. The three lands - Diagon Alley, Hogwarts, and the Forbidden Forest - will expand the Warner Bros. World the park by 678,000 square feet and feature all-new, exclusive Harry Potter-themed rides, created especially for the park.

In advance of today's announcement, Miral and Warner Bros. Discovery invited me to interview Miral CEO Dr. Mohamed Abdalla Al Zaabi and Warner Bros. Discovery President Global Experiences & Studio Operations Simon Robinson about the park's expansion. The interview was conducted via email.


Robinson, left, and Dr. Al Zaabi. Photos courtesy Miral

Robert: The Wizarding World of Harry Potter has welcomed fans all over the world to Warner Bros. Studio Tours and Universal theme parks. What opportunities do you see for your teams to develop unique experiences at Warner Bros. World on Yas Island that will entice fans to visit this new area?

Robinson: Warner Bros. World Abu Dhabi offers fans something truly unique. As the world's largest indoor theme park, located on one of the world's premier entertainment destinations, it provides an opportunity to experience multiple Warner Bros. franchises in one place. The addition of Harry Potter is especially significant as these will be a first in the Middle East.

The opportunity for our teams is to create something that feels authentic to the wizarding world while also being uniquely part of the Warner Bros. World Abu Dhabi experience. We're not simply building attractions, we're continuing to evolve a destination where fans can immerse themselves in the stories, characters and worlds they love in new and memorable ways.

For fans across the region, and for those traveling from around the world, the chance to explore iconic locations such as Diagon Alley, Hogwarts and the Forbidden Forest, alongside other beloved Warner Bros. franchises under one roof, will make this a truly distinctive experience. That's what we're focused on delivering: a world-class destination that gives fans compelling reasons to visit, return, and create lasting memories.

Robert: This will be the first themed area at Warner Bros. World Yas Island, Abu Dhabi based on a live-action Warner Bros. Discovery franchise, rather than an animated one. What opportunities and challenges does that create for the design team?

Robinson: Harry Potter is one of the most beloved franchises in the world, with a deeply passionate and committed fanbase spanning multiple generations. As with anything related to Harry Potter, expectations are incredibly high, and meeting those expectations is both a privilege and a responsibility.

One of the biggest opportunities for us is to create environments that feel authentic, immersive and true to Harry Potter, while seamlessly becoming part of the broader Warner Bros. World Abu Dhabi experience. Fans have an incredibly strong connection to these locations, stories and characters, so it's important that what we create feels both familiar and new.

At the same time, that's also the challenge. Expectations for Harry Potter are extraordinarily high, and fans know every detail of this world. Our job is to honor what they love about the franchise while creating experiences that surprise and delight them.

That's the balance we're striving for: delivering something that is unmistakably Harry Potter, while creating a world-class experience that can only be found at Warner. Bros. World Abu Dhabi.

Robert: How do you accommodate the wide range of Harry Potter fans when designing experiences for this new area?

Robinson: One of the things that makes Harry Potter so special is the breadth of its fanbase. On the one hand, you have lifelong fans who grew up with the books and films, parents now sharing those stories with their children, and on the other, entirely new generations discovering the wizarding world for the first time.

When we're designing experiences, we start with the guest in mind. Our goal is to create something that feels authentic for the most passionate fans, while also being accessible, welcoming and magical for families and first-time visitors.

That means paying close attention to the details that fans know and love, while creating experiences that anyone can enjoy, regardless of how familiar they are with the franchise.

If we can create moments that resonate with dedicated fans while inspiring new ones, then we've done our job.

Robert: How does Harry Potter fit into the growing brand portfolio on Yas Island?

Dr. Al Zaabi: Bringing the Harry Potter franchise to Yas Island is a first for the Middle East and one that reinforces our commitment to delivering immersive, world-class experiences that contribute to the evolution of the island. It marks a major milestone in our long-standing partnership with Warner Bros. Discovery Global Experiences, demonstrating our joint efforts to elevating Yas Island�s global appeal by bringing globally recognized stories and characters to life through immersive experiences.

Alongside the recently-opened Kryptonite Collider and the upcoming Superman Up and Away roller coaster [debuting in 2028 - Robert], the three Harry Potter�themed lands are part of the expansion of Warner Bros. World Yas Island, Abu Dhabi that will add approximately 70,000 square meters of theme park space, increasing its footprint by more than 50%. This expansion aims to significantly contribute to extending visitor length of stay as well as increasing cross-visitation on Yas Island.

Robert: What new fans are you hoping to attract to the park and to Abu Dhabi by bringing Harry Potter-themed Lands to the park?

Dr. Al Zaabi: Harry Potter is one of the most enduring franchises in modern entertainment history and resonates with fans who grew up with the novels and films just as it does with younger audiences discovering the wizarding world for the first time.

By introducing an experience of this scale, calibre and significance on Yas Island, we are expanding the destination�s appeal to further attract loyal fans of the franchise who plan entire travel itineraries around world-class themed experiences, alongside families, thrill-seekers, cultural explorers and business travelers.

Ultimately, our goal is to reinforce Yas Island�s position as a leading global leisure and entertainment destinations while strengthening Abu Dhabi�s appeal as a world-class tourism destination and playing a major role in the diversification of the Emirate�s economy. This is also aligned with our commitment to Abu Dhabi�s Tourism Strategy to attract 39.3 million visitors and create 178,000 jobs by the end of 2030, increasing the sector�s contribution to non-oil GDP.

Robert: How will the introduction of Harry Potter-themed Lands affect other attractions and experiences on Yas Island and in Abu Dhabi?

Dr. Al Zaabi: At Miral, we approach Yas Island as an integrated ecosystem. Our overarching strategy is anchored in seamless world-class guest experiences with attractions in close proximity, creating a multiplier effect.

With Yas Island�s proximity to Zayed International Airport, Saadiyat Cultural District, and other key leisure and cultural attractions, our guests transition seamlessly between cultural landmarks, theme parks, luxury beachfronts, dining, and event venues. An expansion of this magnitude naturally elevates the end-to-end journey as part of our ongoing efforts to curate a cohesive and frictionless guest journey.

This ecosystem model has been key in the island�s year-on-year growth, with new attractions lengthening the average stay and elevating overall hotel performance on Yas Island and across Abu Dhabi. In 2025, Yas Island recorded 44 million visits, a significant 16 per cent increase compared to 2024, with hotel occupancy averaging 84 per cent, and a 16 per cent increase in ADR compared to 2024.

Robert: We know that the past several months have brought challenges for the UAE and travel to the region. What would you like to say to fans around the world who have been wondering about visiting Abu Dhabi and perhaps Warner Bros. World Yas Island, Abu Dhabi in the near future?

Dr. Al Zaabi: The UAE�s strength is built on long-term vision, thoughtful planning and strong foundations to ensure resilience and stability. Guided by the UAE�s leadership, we remain focused on safely delivering joyful and memorable immersive experiences. Our theme parks continue to operate seamlessly while we advance our development plans.

Over the past year alone, we delivered Yas Bay East Beach, a contemporary coastal escape for adults seeking a relaxed yet vibrant atmosphere; opened the latest expansion at Yas Waterworld, adding 11 new rides, slides and attractions; and in July, we welcomed our first guests to experience the exhilarating Kryptonite Collider at Warner Bros. World Abu Dhabi. Meanwhile, we are on track with our pipeline, which, as well as the Harry Potter themed lands, set for construction completion in 2029, also includes the upcoming Superman Up and Away roller coaster, set for completion in 2028.

To our guests, fans, and future visitors worldwide, Abu Dhabi remains one of the world�s safest, most welcoming, and forward-looking destinations. Featuring an unparalleled blend of leisure, entertainment, culture, sport, dining, retail, and hospitality experiences, our indoor, climate-controlled attractions welcome guests and visitors throughout the year. We look forward to welcoming the world to Abu Dhabi to experience the Harry Potter-themed lands at Warner Bros. World Yas Island once it�s open.

Update from Robert: Miral is sharing a new hype video for the expansion, which offers what I think is a giant clue as to what one of the new rides will be.

title: Rope Drop: What will Six Flags announce this week?
summary:
By Robert Niles: As the "rope drop" starts a day at theme parks, the Sunday "Rope Drop" post kicks off the week here at Theme Park Insider. Here is what lies ahead for fans at the parks this week.

Six Flags is promising announcements on Monday and Tuesday this week. The first will address making experiences "more accessible for families," while the second will "reinforce Six Flags' position as the home of world-class thrills," according to the company's media rep. Those announcements are in addition to the latest promise of an announcement from Six Flags Magic Mountain about its Vekoma Thrill Glider coaster, which is set for Thursday.

At Walt Disney World, the new Magic of Disney Animation pavilion at Disney's Hollywood Studios opens officially on September 14, but Disney will be hosting a media preview on Wednesday, so check us after that for coverage.

Friday, SeaWorld opens its annual Howl-O-Scream haunt event in Orlando, San Diego, and San Antonio. The event runs select nights through Halloween in Orlando and San Diego, with one extra night on November 1 in San Antonio.

On Saturday, Hong Kong Disneyland celebrates its 21st birthday. The park debuted September 12, 2005.

Planning a trip?

Several attractions go down for refurb at Disneyland this week and next. Here are the current refurbishment schedules from Disneyland, Walt Disney World and Universal Orlando.

September 8: Indiana Jones Adventure closes at Disneyland, with no reopening date.
September 8-11: Mark Twain Riverboat closes at Disneyland.
September 14: Mad Tea Party closes at Disneyland, with no reopening date.
September 14-16: Tom Sawyer Island closes at Disneyland.
September 15-20: The Untrainable Dragon closes at Universal Epic Universe.
September 21-24: Sailing Ship Columbia closes at Disneyland.
October 26: Volcano Bay closes for the season, with a planned return on or before April 1, 2027.
November 2: Tiana's Bayou Adventure closes at Walt Disney World's Magic Kingdom, with no reopening date.
November 20: Jurassic Park River Adventure reopens at Islands of Adventure.
January 4 - February 2, 2027: Popeye & Bluto's Bilge-Rat Barges closes at Islands of Adventure.
January 25 - February 4, 2027: Fyre Drill closes at Universal Epic Universe.
February 8-19, 2027: Harry Potter and the Forbidden Journey closes at Islands of Adventure.

title: Walk Time: Celebrating the last weeks of summer
summary:
By Robert Niles: In theme parks and entertainment, "walk time" is the name for the final paid minutes of your shift, when you gather your stuff and start heading home. At Theme Park Insider, "Walk Time" is our weekend look back at the past seven days in theme park news.

Universal Studios Hollywood set its official opening date for Fast & Furious: Hollywood Drift - September 16, just making the coaster's promised "summer" opening by a few days. Meanwhile, the park opened its 2026 edition of Halloween Horror Nights, with a spectacular "Sinner" house and two original concepts leading this year's line-up of haunted houses. We talked about Orlando's HHN debut on the podcast this week and then welcomed industry legend Bob Rogers, who shared some of the secrets of creating emotionally resonant attractions, which he details in his new book, "Deep Story."

In other roller coaster news, Six Flags Magic Mountain's promised announcement this week about its next attraction turned out to be an announcement of announcement. Maybe we will get the actual announcement on Thursday? Or, maybe not.

We also are expecting more news following the Arie family's announcement this week that it has sold the ArieForce One roller coaster and that the highly-rated RMC creation will be moving to a new (undisclosed) home.

Efteling this week announced that its new Raveleijn show, Raveleijn: Battle for the City, will open December 1, along with the new Ravenring ride. Efteling is spending �10 million on the new show, which it is producing in collaboration with Puy du Fou.

As one production prepares for its debut, another is getting ready to call a wrap. Universal Orlando announced this week that its Animal Actors show close November 2. The show was one of the few remaining opening day attractions from Universal Studios Florida, with only ET and the Horror Makeup Show (which is closed until this winter for a rewrite) still going.

In personnel news this week, Liseberg has appointed Amanda Rydenstam as its new Creative Director, succeeding David Schofield. She joins Liseberg from her role as Creative Director at Okidoki Architects.

Storyland Studios has named Adam Moore as the firm's first-ever Vice President of Story. He comes to Storyland from from�Walt Disney Animation Studios, following his role as Chair of the Department of Cinematic Arts Cal State Long Beach.

The Themed Entertainment Association this week honored its 2026 TEA Masters, "honoring themed entertainment professionals whose careers have made significant and lasting contributions to the global industry." This year's honorees are AOA co-founder Tom Acomb, Universal Creative's Eric Baker and Patrice Ragusa, Groupe F's Christophe Berthonneau, Animal Repair Shop's Susan Bonds, RWS Global's Paul Kent, and KirPaint founder Kirsten Ruhs.

title: Sinners, original IP lead the way at Horror Nights Hollywood
summary:
By Jacob Sundstrom: If I may start my review of Halloween Horror Nights Hollywood 2026 with a mea culpa. For years, I�ve been adamant that what makes Horror Nights Hollywood is its impressive lineup of haunted houses based on movies, TV shows and music you love. This commitment to intellectual property (IP) helped Horror Nights stand out in a market dominated by Knott�s Scary Farm.

And there�s still something special, even magical, about what Horror Nights Hollywood pulled off with Sinners, the haunted house recreating Ryan Coogler�s Oscar-winning masterpiece. But in 2026, Horror Nights Hollywood showed it can make magic happen without any IP at all; Dead, Deader, Deadest might be my favorite house of the year, and the Latin American monsters house of the year, Killcea�era, is very strong.

So uh, maybe Horror Nights Hollywood should do more non-IP houses if these are the results. We�ve moved past the era of black wall transitions that haunted Horror Nights Hollywood for years. But in its place, the slate of IP houses has grown increasingly stale. Killer Klownz From Outer Space is back for the third time in recent memory and Stranger Things returns less as a recap of Season 5 (thank god) and more of an ode to demogorgons and Vecna.


Vecna in the Stranger Things 5 house. All photos by Noelle Sundstrom

But let�s circle back to Sinners, which is a signature achievement for Horror Nights Hollywood. Located in the former year-round Walking Dead Attraction space, Sinners makes full use of its permanent environment beginning with a spectacular show scene inside Club Juke. Horror Nights cleverly leaves one more set of switchbacks for us to navigate in this room, allowing all guests to see Smoke and Stack welcome us to their club.

Naturally, things go horribly wrong from there. Horror Nights brought Sinners� vampires to life, complete with glowing eyes, while hitting many of the action beats from the film. It�s no replacement for watching the movie, of course, but it�s the type of visceral excitement that you can only get from live theater.

How about Dead, Deader, Deadest? The setting is simple: You enter a mortuary where something sinister is taking place. This is a beautifully dressed house, especially the foyer that serves as the entryway. You can watch the full walkthrough if you�d like spoilers, but I was particularly impressed by how the park conveyed your walk into the freezer and the incinerator.

Killcea�era uses a unique hook and framing to reintroduce familiar monsters. Yes, this is basically �Latin American Carrie,� but that works at an event like Horror Nights. She conjures up a roster of monsters that will be familiar, perhaps too familiar, to regular Horror Nights attendees. What I can say is that despite that familiarity, Killcea�era feels fresh.

The Terror Tram features Art the Clown following his tremendously successful debut at the 2025 event. Horror Nights borrows the Christmas motifs from the second film to great success to bring to life the ideal version of Terror Tram. Without the confined spaces to truly be scary, this is an attraction that relies on the personality of its villains and the energy of its performers. Lucky for us, Art the Clown and the performers who portray him have brought plenty of both. [Watch video]


Art the Clown stars in the Terror Tram scare zone

There�s not much new to report from either Killer Klownz nor Stranger Things, though I should note the cast for Klownz was really bringing it on Thursday night. So let�s move on to the other major IP house for 2026, Ozzy Osbourne: Prince of Darkness. This house, thanks in large part to the music, is a lot of fun and features some neat environments. But it doesn�t feel as fully realized as the best Horror Nights houses do. [Watch video]


Ozzy Osbourne: Prince of Darkness

Hellraiser and Evil Dead Burn round out the haunted houses. Hellraiser has a lot of great moments that will take fans back into the trilogy of horror films. But let�s be real: We�re here to see Pinhead and his merry band of sadomasochists monologue at us before jumping out from behind doors, windows and severed heads. The house delivers on that promise. [Watch video]

I imagine Evil Dead Burn has a plot, but I can�t tell you what it is. How much that matters is a matter of taste; suffice to say this is a cursed house chock full of deadites. That will almost certainly get the job done for most Horror Nights attendees. [Watch video]

The Purge: Dangerous Waters returns as the only show, taking over the Waterworld stage for a stunt show that is virtually unchanged from previous editions. Fast and Furious: Hollywood Drift was running, but only for guests with special tickets (VIP tours, some Express pass holders) so I did not get my first chance to get on the new roller coaster. Ah well.

Universal Studios Halloween Horror Nights runs until November 1. Tickets start at $75: Universal Studios Hollywood tickets.
